rationale: The status quo since mid-2025 is Musk realigned with Trump and spending heavily for Republicans, about $366M in total, mostly in the same direction as Trump, for example on Paxton. The closest case is Kentucky Senate. Musk put $10M into a pro-Morris super PAC, and Trump endorsed Barr on May 1, but Morris dropped out and endorsed Barr the same day, so the two backings were never at the same time. Musk never actually funded Massie. Only general elections remain, and divergence there is unlikely. The Kentucky case gives some chance of a YES on the creator's reading.

Cooper leads North Carolina by about 7-14 points (P(R) ~5%), and Flanagan leads Minnesota by about 3 points (P(R) ~18%). Jackson leads Collins in Maine by about 1.5-2.7 points. Collins beat her 2020 polls badly, so she keeps perhaps a 35-40% chance. The three races are correlated through the national environment. The chance that Republicans win at least one is a bit under even.

Runoff polls show Flavio Bolsonaro slightly ahead: Quaest +2, Datafolha +2, MDA +1, PoderData tied, and an average of about Flavio 51.2-48.8 in valid votes. He also led the first round, 47 to 45. That gives Lula about a 30% chance to win. A Lula win would most likely be narrow, with about an 85-90% chance the margin is under 4 points. A news article quoted Polymarket and Kalshi prices for the winner; I ignored them.

Kreiss-Tomkins leads every recent poll after ranked-choice rounds: ASR +8, NYT/Siena +4, Fabrizio/Anzalone +10, RCP average +7. Cook moved the race to Lean D. The case against is that Alaska is Republican-leaning, polls there have historically overstated Democrats, and Cook warns the result will be closer. One search result showed a Polymarket price; I ignored it.

Mid-October reporting says Mojtaba Khamenei has made no verified public appearance and released no new photo, video or audio. His output is written messages only, including one on Oct 17. The only footage is an undated 12-second clip from August, and a viral clip was debunked as old. With 13 days left and months of absence, the base rate is low. Some chance remains of a staged video appearance.

Yisrael Beiteinu polls at about 8 seats. The race for prime minister is between Eisenkot's Yashar (about 22 seats) and Netanyahu's Likud (about 21). Lieberman is a possible kingmaker, not a likely prime minister. A rotation deal naming him first is a remote tail.

In April 2026 the DEA moved FDA-approved marijuana products and state-licensed medical marijuana to Schedule III, effective April 28. Broader rescheduling of all marijuana is still pending after the ALJ hearing and is reportedly paused. Whether the partial order counts as 'marijuana federally rescheduled' is a question of creator interpretation. A full final rule before Nov 3 is unlikely, so the probability rests mostly on whether the April order counts.

Trilateral US-Russia-Ukraine meetings happened several times in 2026, in Abu Dhabi and Geneva, so the base rate for some meeting in a given month is moderate. The US has proposed a technical trilateral by the end of October, and Ukraine agreed. Russia has not publicly confirmed and is escalating strikes, and Ukrainian sources do not expect serious talks before spring. Only 13 days remain and no date or venue is set.

The Houthis took Perim in mid-September. Al Arabiya claimed on Oct 9 that government forces had taken the island. A later AFP report from military sources said government forces had not secured the strait and that Perim remains in Houthi hands. Retaking a defended island by amphibious assault and establishing clear control in 13 days is unlikely. Contested control resolves NO.

The June MOU's 60-day window passed in August with no final deal. Through late September, indirect talks had stalled over the order of steps: Iran wants Hormuz control and sanctions relief first, and the US wants the nuclear file first. Reports in October suggest the ceasefire has frayed and regional actors are urging renewed talks. A signed final deal with measurable nuclear limits within about 6 weeks is a low-probability event.

The polling average gives Peltola a small lead of about 1.4-2.4 points. Ranked-choice final rounds show 50-48 and 51-49, and Sabato rates the race Lean D. Alaska's Republican lean, Sullivan's incumbency and a history of polls overstating Democrats in Alaska keep Sullivan close to even. One search result cited a Kalshi price; I ignored it.

Hobbs, the incumbent Democrat, leads Biggs in all October polls. Margins run from +4 in GQR to +17 in HighGround, with averages of +5 to +11. The national environment appears to favor Democrats. Arizona's narrow history and the spread between pollsters keep this short of a lock.
